value.body: A sound or recording engineer captures and shapes audio, from recording a singer in a studio to mixing a film song or running the sound desk at a concert. Employers include recording studios, film and OTT post-production houses, event companies, radio and podcast producers. A typical day involves setting up equipment, recording takes, and editing or mixing for hours.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: BPA / B.Music, or a diploma in sound engineering

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Digital audio workstations, mixing consoles, microphones

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Most start as studio assistants or live-sound crew, learning on the job. Musical training from a BPA helps with ear and timing; a short audio engineering course fills the technical gaps. A portfolio of mixed tracks is commonly asked for.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Editing and mixing in a DAW

value.title: At a glance
items: Much of the work is freelance or contract-based.
Next roles: mixing or mastering engineer, live sound head, studio owner.
